intent: Add a second, VPN-independent YouTube block in Firefox, and give the phone a backup script covering everything ADB can actually reach before a possible Device Owner factory reset.
scope: Non-goal: app private data -- unreachable without root, documented rather than faked
Non-goal: tamper-resistance; only Device Owner removes the off switch
changes: phone_backup.sh captures package lists (including what was purged for user 0), every third-party APK with its splits, /sdcard user data, all three settings namespaces, and the focus-mode state. It ships a RESTORE-BY-HAND.md naming what it cannot restore, and --verify re-reads the artefacts.
Documented the uBlock Origin layer: the 8 filters, the import procedure, and why `adb shell input text` must not be used to enter them.
Documented measured undo costs for all three layers, including the Play Store finding, so the doc does not overstate the block.

verification.evidence: 54/54 packages, 126 APK files, 5.1 GB, 'Verify OK'. Split APKs captured in full (com.termux has base + 5 split_config). Spot-checked 3 random APKs with unzip -t: all OK. pl.infakt.infakt, pl.mbank, com.kunzisoft.keepass.libre and org.thoughtcrime.securesms all present.

verification.command: force-stop com.celzero.bravedns, then load youtube.com in Firefox
verification.evidence: 'uBlock Origin has prevented the following page from loading: https://m.youtube.com/ ... filter ||youtube.com^ ... found in: My filters'. The layers are independent: killing the VPN does not restore YouTube. Control example.com still loads; VPN restored afterwards.

Google Play shows a live Install button, so the app-removal layer is a ONE-TAP undo -- weaker than the VPN toggle. Not installed; state re-confirmed installed=false. Recorded in the doc rather than left implicit.

risks: The first two runs of phone_backup.sh pulled 1 of 54 and then 6 of 54 APKs. Cause: `while read < file` with `adb` inside the loop -- adb inherits and drains the same stdin. Fixed by reading into an array with mapfile first; the same bug was fixed in the .kdbx loop. verify_backup now compares package-directory count against packages-third-party.txt, because an integrity-only check called the 1-of-54 run a pass.
Backgrounding the script with nohup truncated it mid-run twice; it must be run in the foreground. Not a script defect but worth knowing before trusting an unattended run.

No .kdbx is captured: KeePassDX keeps its database in private storage. Confirmed with the user that the canonical copy lives on the PC, so this is expected here -- downgraded from a warning to an info line, which means a genuinely missing database on some other device would be quieter.

infakt (pl.infakt.infakt) is device-paired for banking ('Usun powiazanie z telefonem') and holds a live session with funds and an active card. The account is server-side so login works on a new device, but the pairing and app PIN do not survive a wipe; re-pairing is via SMS to the number registered in-app. 2FA method (SMS vs authenticator) still unconfirmed by the user.
uBlock filters live in the Firefox profile and are NOT in the backup; they must be re-added by hand after a wipe.
rollback: git revert removes the script and doc changes; no device state is touched by reverting.
Delete a backup directory under ~/phone-backup/ to reclaim space -- each full run is ~5 GB.
Remove the uBlock filters from uBlock dashboard -> My filters and press apply.
